title: Paid Leave Access Declines with Age, Study Finds
discussion_signal: The author describes an ATUS Leave Module study of employed adults ages 55–70, reporting that paid-leave access declines with age and that part-time work may contribute. The discussion extends the finding to older workers, parents, and employer retention, framing leave as income stability and a return-to-work condition rather than only a benefit. The social signal is a possible age/part-time channel through which care and health needs become labor-market fragility.
linked_research_question: Which workers can convert a care or health shock into paid time away, and who instead absorbs the shock through reduced hours, income loss, or exit?
limits: The post summarizes the study and does not provide all estimates or methods
The comments broaden the discussion beyond the studied older-worker population
The relay does not establish that employer leave policy improves retention in this sample
